name: MAC Mobility | Remote EVPN <-> Remote EVPN | Sequence Number Wins
source: gap-analysis:G1 from SW-204115 reference table row 7
status_note: G1 wired 2026-04-21 via Block 3 spirent_evpn_seq_race handler. Three scenarios dispatch to the same handler which calls spirent_inject_evpn_mac_route twice (simulating PE-A then PE-B) with different seq + next-hop values. SC03 additionally calls spirent_withdraw_evpn_mac_route to verify fallback-to-loser behavior. Single Spirent BGP peer simulates both remote PEs via differentiated next-hops.
gap_rationale: The reference table in SW-204115 defines Row 7: EVPN->EVPN (remote-to-remote). When a MAC already known from Remote PE-A via RT-2 is now advertised by Remote PE-B with a higher sequence number, the local PE must accept the new RT-2 and update forwarding. No RT-2 is advertised by the local PE (it does not own the MAC). No suppression applies. No local loop count.

device_requirements.notes: Single Spirent BGP peer simulates 2 remote PEs via different next-hop IPs in RT-2 (not different labels -- that would require dual Spirent sessions). Live-validated approach 2026-04-21.

config_before_test.description: No special config on DUT beyond base EVPN-VPLS SI. Spirent BGP EVPN peer injects RT-2 updates with different next-hop IPs (simulating PE-A/PE-B) and sequence numbers.
config_before_test.spirent_note: Single Spirent BGP peer sends competing RT-2 updates: (1) MAC X with seq=0 nh=<pe_a_ip>, then (2) MAC X with seq=1 nh=<pe_b_ip>. DUT should switch forwarding to pe_b_ip.

scenarios.name: Remote PE-B advertises same MAC with higher seq than PE-A; forwarding switches
scenarios.what_happens: PE-A sends RT-2 for MAC X with seq=0 nh=pe_a_ip. PE-B sends RT-2 for MAC X with seq=1 nh=pe_b_ip. Local PE must prefer PE-B (higher seq wins per RFC 7432 section 15.1).
scenarios.what_cannot_happen: Local PE must NOT advertise its own RT-2 (it does not own the MAC locally). No suppression. No local loop counter increment.

scenarios.name: Equal seq from two PEs; higher IP wins (RFC 7432 tiebreaker)
scenarios.what_happens: When two remote PEs advertise the same MAC with the same sequence number, RFC 7432 says the PE with the higher IP address wins. Verify this tiebreaker.
scenarios.what_cannot_happen: Local PE must not generate any RT-2 of its own. No suppression.

trigger.note: Same seq, higher next-hop IP should win per RFC 7432.

scenarios.name: PE-A (winner) withdraws; PE-B (older, lower seq) takes over as only path
scenarios.what_happens: PE-A sends RT-2 with higher seq (wins). PE-B sends RT-2 with lower seq (loses). Then PE-A withdraws. PE-B must become the installed path because it is the only remaining advertisement.
scenarios.what_cannot_happen: MAC should not become unreachable. No ghost MAC.

trigger.note: Handler: spirent_evpn_seq_race -- inject PE-A (winner, seq=1), inject PE-B (loser, seq=0), then withdraw PE-A. PE-B becomes installed path.

pe_a_ip.notes: Spirent BGP peer LDP loopback simulating PE-A. Must be MPLS-reachable on DUT.

pe_b_ip.notes: Second next-hop used by handler to simulate PE-B. Does not require a second Spirent session -- same peer, different nh value.
